payload.headline: statvault.org had been serving S269 build for three days and four separately-justified gates all declined to report it
payload.rootCause: A test spawned the real handshake builder with cwd: process.cwd(), rewriting a tracked artifact another test in the same suite asserts is fresh. Under --test-concurrency=2 the suite was a coin flip (2 failures vs 2200/2200, same commit, ten minutes apart); the Hetzner release lane runs it before promoting.
transferableLessons: A gate INVOCATION is a claim separate from its existence, caller, reject-capability and declared mode - a blocking step invoked without --strict cannot exit non-zero however well its core is proven
Exempt a gate failure by REASON, never by the NAME of the step that reported it - a step aggregating several reasons exempts them all
A wall-clock TTL is only evidence about state that can change without a commit; a committed content-hashed snapshot does not decay on a clock
Two ends agreeing is not truth when neither is derived from what they describe - deriving a field beats making a doc quote it verbatim
A test must never write the repo it tests; enforce by diffing tracked-file state across the run, not by scanning for one spelling
A fix in CODE and a protocol that names a PATH are two surfaces - closing one leaves the other pointing where it always did

payload.headline: Three-day production freeze traced to a Node version gap between the dev machine (v24) and the release box (v20.20.2); deployed and verified live
payload.rootCause: S270 single-sourced a module as .ts and had the .mjs scripts lane import it via Node native type-stripping. The release box runs Node v20.20.2 which has none, so ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION failed node-core on every validation run and, via the prebuild lifecycle, the production image build too.
payload.fix: Re-hosted the single source as .cjs + .d.cts. Three formats were needed: .ts fails on Node 20; .mjs fails in Jest which treats every .mjs as native ESM regardless of transform; .cjs satisfies plain Node (cjs-module-lexer), Jest, webpack and tsc --noEmit with allowJs still false.
transferableLessons: Measure a runtime-level feature against the machine that must RUN it, not the one you are standing on - ask the box, it answers in one SSH call
When a remote lane fails, read that lane own log before concluding why; a local repro proves a defect exists, never that it is the one you are looking at
A guard that subtracts pre-existing dirt reports purity on a dirty dev tree and the truth in CI - validate that shape once on a clean tree before quoting its green
A gate INVOCATION is a claim separate from its existence, caller, reject-capability and declared mode
Exempt a gate failure by REASON not by the NAME of the step that reported it, and require disclosure rather than silence

payload.pattern: redact() blanket-masks any loaded secret-list value >=8 chars anywhere it appears in output text, with no entropy/uniqueness check. A completely non-secret, common literal (NODE_ENV=production from an unrelated sibling projects env file, loaded into the shared cross-project redact list) matched the word production inside a JSON receipt, corrupting a downstream release-truth court into a false NO-GO even though the underlying state was correctly verified.
payload.solution: Add a minimum-entropy or allowlist check to redact() so common non-secret literals (env-mode words like production/staging/development, short common words) are never added to the shared redact list, or scope the redact list per-capability instead of merging every sibling project env file into one global list.
